Our ideal hire has a builder mindset, is detail oriented, action oriented and proactive. They own their role and continuously help identify ways to improve operations processes and controls. It is essential that this person manages time well, keeps on top of deliverables, and has the potential to grow with us. Experience in credit products, prepaid cards or other spend operations functions is a strong plus. 

 

We manage billions of dollars, so the stakes are high. We want to deliver extraordinary experiences that meet our client's on-demand expectations, while being a compliance leader. At Wealthsimple, we are maker-owners, we believe that simplicity is better, and we do what's right for each client.

 - Data & analytics: Has a strong proficiency in SQL, and a history of using data to answer complex problems. Ability to translate business requirements into technical reporting solutions.

 - Stakeholder Management: Experience with complex reporting processes and stakeholder requirements, with proven ability to deliver financial reports to senior leadership and various business units.

Required Qualifications

 - 3+ years of experience in financial analysis or similar role

 - Advanced proficiency in SQL and Excel

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.
 Toast International is building its upmarket business across the UK & Ireland, Canada, and Australia, focused on restaurant groups with 16 to 500 locations. We're hiring a solutions leader to own the technical side of every International deal over 15 locations. Your demos and labs are where our deals are won or lost. You'll start as a player-coach, carrying deals yourself, and you'll build the International upmarket solutions team as the business grows.
 About this role: 
 Run demos that win the room. Build every demo from discovery. Show a 40-site group their own menu, their own workflows and the systems they already run, in their market's version of the product. Tailor it to each person in the buying group, from the head of ops to the IT lead to finance. Leave each of them with a reason to champion Toast.
 Run labs that end in a decision. Agree success criteria with the customer before the lab starts. Build and maintain the lab environment, track every issue, drive escalations and root cause analysis, and close the lab with a clear yes or no. No lab ends without an agreed next step.
 Own the technical outcome through go-live. The deal isn't won until the customer is live and it matches what we sold. Stay involved through procurement and handoff.
 Architect the solution. Design how Toast fits into a multi-location group's existing stack:
 ERP, payroll and HR (e.g. Workday)
 Inventory, loyalty, gift card processors and kiosks
 Delivery and custom integrations
 Network and hardware
 Multi-entity and franchise structures, and data migration
 All of it within what's actually available, and what payments rules allow, in each market.
 Lead security, IT and compliance reviews. Own vendor security questionnaires, PCI scoping conversations and the technical sections of RFPs.
 Speak product's language. Write BRDs that product and engineering can act on: the problem, the customer's own words, workarounds tried, what's at stake across the segment (not just one account), and options with tradeoffs. Turn one customer's ask into a case for the platform.
 Present the roadmap with credibility. Walk executive and IT audiences through what exists, what's coming and what isn't, without overpromising. Keep their trust when the answer is "not yet."
 Sell outcomes, not features. Partner with sales to build the business case. Translate technical fit into the outcomes the economic buyer cares about, such as labor, speed of service and revenue. When a buyer is weighing a feature gap, help them see it against the full value of the platform, and make sure their IT team feels heard along the way.
 Engineer workarounds, and know when to hold the line. Design and document solutions to complex gaps, and judge when a workaround creates debt we'll pay for at go-live.
 Build real relationships outside the sales thread. Become the trusted counterpart to the customer's IT lead, head of operations and systems owners, relationships that hold up on their own merit.
 Hand off cleanly. Give onboarding and implementation a clear record of what was promised, what was configured and why, so delivery matches the sale.
 Build the function. Set the engagement model for when and how AEs bring you in, qualify technical fit early and disqualify fast, and build reusable assets: demo environments for each market, reference architectures, an RFP library and BRD standards.
 Partner across Solutions. Work closely with the International SMB Solutions team on clear lanes, shared tools and cross-coverage.
 Grow the team. Help define, hire and develop the International upmarket solutions team as the business scales.
 Own your own leverage. Continuously find the repetitive parts of the role (RFP answers, security questionnaires, discovery notes, demo resets) and systematically get them off your plate.
 Close the loop on what's broken. Feed product gaps, lost-deal reasons and market differences back to product and sales leadership, so the next deal is easier than the last.
 Do you have the right ingredients: 
 An elite demo and lab track record. You've run tailored demos for multi-stakeholder buying committees and taken complex labs or pilots to a signed decision. In the interview, you'll run a demo for us and walk us through a lab you ran end to end.
 You build and maintain your own environments. Demo data, lab configurations and resets are your job, done fast and adapted for each market.
 7+ years in solutions architecture, solutions engineering or technical consulting, with at least 4 supporting mid-market or enterprise deals with 6 to 12+ month cycles and buying committees.
 Experience in hospitality, retail or payments technology serving multi-location operators.
 You've taken complex deals through lab or pilot to go-live. You can walk us through one end to end, including what went wrong and what you changed.
 Integration fluency: REST APIs, webhooks, authentication and data flows. You can read API docs and sketch an architecture on a whiteboard. Coding isn't required, but you can test your own assumptions.
 Security and compliance fluency: PCI DSS scope, and privacy regimes such as UK GDPR, PIPEDA and the Australian Privacy Act. You're comfortable owning a security review.
 Writing that product teams act on. Bring a sanitized requirements doc, solution design or BRD to the interview.
 Executive presence with C-suite and IT leaders, including delivering "no" and keeping the relationship.
 You've mentored or led SEs, or built a presales process from scratch, and you want to build a team.
 International experience across more than one market or regulatory regime. Willing to travel across the UK & Ireland, Canada and Australia (30%+).
 Comfort working in build mode, where territory definition, process and tooling are actively being shaped and you're expected to have an opinion on them.
 Special Sauce (non-essential skills, nice to have): 
 Hands-on experience with enterprise POS or hospitality platforms in these markets
 ERP, HR or workforce management integration experience
 MEDDPICC
 What success looks like in year one 
 Every 16+ location deal gets a tailored demo, and every lab has agreed success criteria and ends in a decision.
 Deals we win go live on the timeline we agreed. No stalls, no churn, no post-sale surprises.
 AEs know exactly when and how to bring you in, and technical fit is settled early in the cycle, not in week ten.
 Product changes a decision because of a BRD you wrote.
 A clear plan for the next upmarket solutions hire.

We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them.  Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’EDC ! 
 À EDC, nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Nous leur offrons les outils financiers et l’expertise dont elles ont besoin pour explorer de nouveaux marchés et réduire les risques, dans un seul but : bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce. #LI-Hybrid
 Poste : Gestionnaire, Gestion du risque de modélisation
 Type d’emploi : Affectation permanente
 Détails de la rémunération : 
 Gest., Analyse quantitative 19 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 112 006 $ à 149 341 $ en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience, plus une rémunération au rendement. 
 Lieu de travail: 
 Exportation et développement Canada applique un modèle de travail hybride selon lequel les employés sont tenus de travailler au bureau trois jours par semaine. 
 La personne choisie peut travailler à partir du siège social d’EDC à Ottawa ou à partir du Carrefour communautaire à Toronto à Montréal. 
 Une aide à la réinstallation est offerte aux candidats et candidates admissibles.  
 Candidats internes, veuillez consulter la page Service Now intitulée « Mouvements internes - ce que vous devez savoir ». 
 À propos d’EDC 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. En tant que société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer.
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce.
 Conciliation travail-vie personnelle : EDC offre un régime concurrentiel en ce qui concerne la rémunération et la conciliation travail-vie personnelle : différentes options de travail hybride, trois à quatre semaines de vacances, une période de fermeture, des vendredis d’été raccourcis et les vendredis sans réunion.
 Perfectionnement professionnel : Profitez de nos occasions d’apprentissage continu, notamment des programmes de formation, des ateliers et de la formation linguistique.
 Culture inclusive : Intégrez un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif qui lutte pour l’équité en matière d’emploi et valorise la diversité des idées, des forces et des origines pour favoriser la réussite.
 Programmes de bien-être : Nous offrons des initiatives de bien-être, de l’aide à la santé mentale et des programmes de conditionnement physique pour veiller à votre santé et à votre bonheur.
 Investissement dans la collectivité : Participez à des activités de bénévolat et donnez au suivant grâce à un éventail de programmes de responsabilité sociale.
 Aperçu de l’équipe : 
 L’Équipe de gestion du risque de modélisation assure la supervision, à l’échelle d’EDC, des risques associés aux modèles ainsi qu’aux autres outils utilisés à EDC. Elle établit et tient à jour les politiques de gouvernance, les normes, les procédures, les inventaires, les évaluations des risques et les rapports qui favorisent une gestion rigoureuse du cycle de vie des modèles. En outre, elle valide et examine de manière indépendante les modèles pour s’assurer qu’ils demeurent adaptés à l’usage auquel ils sont destinés. L’Équipe est également à la tête de programmes de gouvernance en évolution visant des outils non associés aux modèles et des modèles d’IA générative. Elle collabore avec les fonctions sectorielles, technologiques, de gestion des risques et de gouvernance pour établir des exigences pratiques et fondées sur les risques, conformes au mandat d’EDC et aux directives réglementaires applicables. 
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 La personne choisie dirigera une équipe de spécialistes du risque de modélisation et supervisera les activités indépendantes de validation, de gestion et de production des rapports liées aux modèles au sein d’EDC. Elle apportera un regard critique et pertinent sur le développement et l’utilisation des modèles, traduira les attentes réglementaires en contrôles concrets et conseillera les parties prenantes des échelons supérieurs sur le risque de modélisation, les limites et les priorités en matière de mesures correctives. Son leadership renforcera les pratiques d’EDC en matière de risque de modélisation et favorisera l’utilisation sûre et efficace des modèles et des technologies d’analyse émergentes. 
 Diriger, encadrer et former une équipe de spécialistes du risque de modélisation, établir les priorités et maintenir des normes élevées en matière de qualité des analyses, de documentation et de respect des délais. 
 Planifier et superviser des validations et des examens de modèles, de manière indépendante et selon une approche fondée sur le risque, dans l’ensemble des domaines de risque et d’activité concernés, notamment le risque de crédit, le risque financier, les prévisions, la tarification, l’évaluation, le capital, la simulation de crise et les analyses avancées. 
 Évaluer la conception des modèles, leur solidité conceptuelle, la qualité des données, la mise en œuvre, le rendement, les limites, les contrôles et la surveillance continue, et transmettre des conclusions et des recommandations claires. 
 Proposer des critiques constructives aux développeurs, propriétaires et utilisateurs de modèles, et superviser la détection, l’escalade hiérarchique et la correction rapide des anomalies révélées par les modèles et des acceptations du risque. 
 Assurer la mise à jour et l’amélioration des politiques, normes, procédures, inventaires, méthodologies de notation des risques et rapports de gestion relatifs au risque de modélisation, conformément à l’appétit pour le risque d’EDC et aux attentes réglementaires applicables. 
 Surveiller le profil de risque de modélisation et préparer des rapports concis ainsi que des recommandations à l’intention de la haute direction et des comités de gouvernance. 
 Conseiller les parties prenantes sur les exigences relatives au cycle de vie des modèles, les nouveaux cas d’utilisation des modèles, les modèles tiers, les risques liés à l’intelligence artificielle et à l’apprentissage automatique, ainsi que sur les approches de gouvernance proportionnelles. 
 Établir des relations fructueuses entre les équipes sectorielles et les fonctions de contrôle, et apporter son soutien aux contrôles réglementaires, aux vérifications internes et aux autres activités d’assurance liées au risque de modélisation. 
 Promouvoir l’amélioration continue grâce à des méthodes, des outils, des données, une automatisation et un partage des connaissances plus efficaces tout en préservant l’indépendance de la fonction de gestion du risque de modélisation. 
 Ce que nous cherchons: 
 Diplôme de premier cycle dans une discipline quantitative comme la statistique, les mathématiques, l’économie, les finances, l’actuariat, l’informatique, l’ingénierie ou un domaine connexe, ou combinaison équivalente d’études et d’expérience 
 Au moins 7 années d’expérience progressive en gestion du risque de modélisation, en validation des modèles, en élaboration de modèles, en gestion des risques quantitatifs ou dans un domaine étroitement lié au sein d’une institution financière ou d’un environnement réglementé 
 Expérience avérée en matière de gestion d’équipes, de projets complexes ou d’un portefeuille d’examens simultanés de modèles, tout en assumant la responsabilité de la qualité, du respect des délais et des résultats attendus par les parties prenantes 
 Solide connaissance de la gouvernance du risque de modélisation et du cycle de vie des modèles, notamment la reconnaissance des modèles, la notation des risques, la validation, l’approbation, la mise en œuvre, le suivi, la gestion des changements et la mise hors service 
 Solides connaissances en analyse quantitative et en statistique; capacité à évaluer les méthodologies, les hypothèses, les données, la mise en œuvre et le rendement des modèles pour tout un éventail de types de modèles 
 Maîtrise des attentes réglementaires du secteur financier canadien et des pratiques du secteur en matière de gestion du risque de modélisation, notamment la Ligne directrice E-23 du Bureau du surintendant des institutions financières (BSIF) et les considérations connexes relatives à la gouvernance, aux données et aux risques technologiques 
 Excellent jugement, bon esprit critique et solides compétences en communication écrite et orale, et capacité à expliquer des questions techniques complexes et à convaincre les parties prenantes des échelons supérieurs 
 Capacité à établir des relations fructueuses tout en conservant son indépendance, son objectivité et son esprit critique 
 Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale en français et en anglais 
 Ce qui vous distinguera : 
 Diplôme d’études supérieures dans une discipline quantitative ou commerciale 
 Titre professionnel (p. ex. CFA, FRM, PRM ou CPA) ou titre d’actuaire 
 Expérience dans le domaine des modèles de risque de crédit, notamment la probabilité de défaut, la perte en cas de défaut et l’exposition en cas de défaut; maîtrise du modèle de pertes de crédit attendues (IFRS 9), de la simulation de crise, du capital économique, de l’évaluation, des prévisions ou des modèles de tarification 
 Expérience dans l’évaluation de l’intelligence artificielle, de l’apprentissage automatique, de l’IA générative ou de modèles tiers, ainsi que des risques associés en matière d’explicabilité, d’équité, de données, de rendement et de gouvernance 
 Maîtrise pratique des outils d’analyse ou des langages de programmation comme Python, R, SAS, SQL ou des technologies comparables 
 Expérience dans l’amélioration des cadres de gouvernance des modèles, la mise en œuvre de changements réglementaires ou la conduite de transformations en matière de processus, de données ou de technologies au sein d’une fonction de gestion du risque de modélisation 
 Connaissances dans les domaines du crédit à l’exportation, des prêts commerciaux, de l’assurance, du financement du commerce ou de l’environnement commercial d’EDC 
 Admissibilité : 
 EDC s'engage à respecter des pratiques d'emploi équitables et la préférence sera accordée aux candidats qui sont en mesure de travailler légalement au Canada au moment de la présentation de leur candidature (citoyens canadiens ou résidents permanents). Les candidats doivent satisfaire aux exigences de sécurité du gouvernement. Pour obtenir de plus amples renseignements, veuillez consulter la section 2.1 de la Norme d’acquisition des talents, accessible sur LINK sous l’onglet Ressources, dans la section Politiques et procédures. Le poste est ouvert aux personnes qui répondent à toutes les exigences essentielles énoncées ci-dessus et dont la candidature est reçue avant la date limite. 
 Engagement d’EDC envers l’équité en matière d’emploi 
 Exportation et développement Canada (EDC) s’engage à favoriser l’équité en matière d’emploi et à constituer une main-d’œuvre diversifiée. Elle s’engage à créer un environnement sûr et inclusif qui respecte les personnes de toutes les origines, aptitudes et compétences. EDC favorise une culture d’inclusion et d’appartenance où chaque personne a des chances égales de se perfectionner, de se développer, de réussir et de réaliser son plein potentiel. 
 Votre candidature doit démontrer clairement que vous répondez à toutes les exigences. Nous remercions tous les candidats de l'intérêt qu'ils portent à une carrière à EDC. Toutefois, seules les personnes sélectionnées pour un entretien seront contactées. Veuillez noter que les candidats qualifiés peuvent être pris en considération pour des postes similaires à ce niveau au sein d'EDC.
 EDC reconnaît que le fait de divulguer la nécessité de prévoir des mesures d’adaptation peut être une question personnelle. Sachez qu’en tant qu’organisation, nous nous engageons à respecter la confidentialité et à veiller à ce que toutes les mesures d’adaptation fournies soient adaptées à vos besoins. Notre objectif est de vous garantir une expérience positive et satisfaisante tout au long du processus de recrutement. N’hésitez donc pas à nous contacter directement pour toute demande d’adaptation à l’adresse accessibility@edc.ca . Nous sommes là pour vous aider à chaque étape du processus.
 Énoncé de confidentialité 
 En postulant à cet emploi, vous reconnaissez avoir lu et compris l'Énoncé de confidentialité d’EDC pour les candidats à l’emploi , qui décrit comment nous recueillons, utilisons, conservons et protégeons les renseignements personnels pendant le processus de recrutement, ainsi que vos droits d’accès et de rectification.

 10+ years of experience in B2B marketing, with deep, recognized expertise and authority in demand generation.

Copywriter & Creative Strategist 
 Write the video ads that bring every new client into Limitless. 
 Location: Remote, United states, Canada, UK
 Team: Limitless Agency, Marketing & Creative
 Employment Type: Paid trial projects, then full-time
 Pay: $5,500 USD/month to start; $7,000 USD/month at full scope
 Primary Focus: All B2B and organic copy: ads, concepts, email, and content
 Also Owns: Quality on our AI-written student copy
 Reports To: Limitless founders
 About Limitless Agency 
 Limitless Agency is a coaching and build program for digital marketing agency owners. Our students run their own agencies, usually doing $40,000 to $100,000 a month. They come to us stuck: lead flow is inconsistent, they are the bottleneck in their own business, and what they have built is not sellable.
 We fix that over a 16-week engagement. Together with our students, we rebuild their acquisition system: ads, funnels, pipelines, automations, copy, and sales scripts. The program includes weekly live implementation calls, a private Slack with the founders, and quarterly workshops in Tampa.
 Both founders have built and scaled agencies of their own, and one of them sold. We have installed these systems in more than 250 agencies, and 50 of those have passed $100,000 a month.
 The Opportunity 
 Paid ads are the entire front end of this business. Every new client comes from a Meta ad, and right now the founders write every one of them. That is the constraint this role exists to solve.
 Put simply: if it is copy in our B2B marketing or our organic content, it runs through this seat.
 What You'll Do 
 Write our paid ad scripts. Deliver at least three new Meta video ad scripts every week, written alongside the founders. Some are filmed in-house; the rest go out to UGC creators. We want more creative in market, and we want it to be good.
 Bring new concepts. Great scripts on tired angles still lose. You will constantly look for what is working in organic feeds, other people's ads, and adjacent markets, then bring us new concepts and formats for delivering our message, not just better scripts for the ones we already run.
 Write organic and YouTube content. Create short-form scripts and posts for the founders' personal brands, plus long-form YouTube scripts and YouTube ads.
 Write email. Produce nurture sequences, broadcasts, and campaign emails for our list.
 Own student copy quality. Our students receive done-for-you ad copy from an AI copywriter we built and trained on scripts that have already produced results. You will review and fine-tune that copy before it reaches students, and keep improving the system so it needs less fine-tuning every month.
 Coach students live. Once a week, you will lead a live copywriting call where students bring their copy and you coach them through making it better.
 Paid ads, organic content, and new concepts are why this seat exists. Student copy quality is a real part of the job, but it is the smaller part.
 Video Scripts Are the Core 
 Video ads are what move the needle in this market, for us and for our students. Static and image ads have their place, but scripts produce the results. That is where most of your time goes, and it is what your work is judged on.
 Writing for spoken video is its own skill. A script that reads well on the page but sounds wrong out loud is a failed script. It has to sound like a real person talking, in the voice of whoever is on camera, with a hook that earns the next three seconds and a structure that holds attention through to the CTA.
 You also bring the creative direction: scene direction, on-screen text, props, formats, and cuts. The person filming needs to know how to shoot the script, not just read it.
 The Leverage Is Already Built 
 Three scripts a week is the floor, not the ceiling, and nobody here grinds that out by hand. You will have access to:
 A library of proven scripts that have already produced results
 Recorded sales calls
 A stack of AI tools and autonomous agents wired into our systems that pull buyer language from sales calls, surface the objections prospects actually raise, and deliver research that would otherwise take days
 We need someone who uses that leverage and still ships work that is genuinely good.
 How We Work 
 Turnaround is measured in days, not weeks. We rarely set deadlines; we pay attention to how fast "right" happens.
 You stay responsive throughout the working day.
 You take feedback quickly and without ego. Copy gets changed, and some gets killed. That is normal here, and it is not personal.
 You learn markets fast. Our buyer is the agency owner, but the student copy you review spans HVAC, gyms, med spas, roofers, law firms, and more. You need to know when it sounds wrong.
 You use AI as leverage, not as a ghostwriter. We expect you to lean on it heavily, but we can tell the difference between a writer using AI as a tool and AI using a writer as a delivery mechanism, and so can our buyers. Part of the job is making our AI copywriter better, not just cleaning up after it.
 Where This Role Goes 
 You start on our paid ad scripts, new concepts, and student copy quality, with organic and YouTube in the mix from the first weeks. As your ads prove out, you take more of the founders' content off their plate.
 There is no fixed waiting period. How fast this happens depends on the quality of your work. If your work is strong early, this moves early.
 Compensation 
 $5,500 USD per month to start, full-time, once you complete the paid trial.
 $7,000 USD per month at full scope: the weekly ad slate, new concepts, organic, and YouTube running without founder rewrites, with student copy quality holding.
 The step up is not based on a subjective review. The targets are written into your offer letter before you sign, so you know exactly what moves you to full scope.
 What Success Looks Like 
 Three or more new ad scripts every week, delivered without anyone chasing you
 The founders filming your scripts instead of rewriting them
 Winning ads in our account that started as your scripts, and at least some that started as your concepts
 Student copy that goes out right the first time, and an AI copywriter that needs less fine-tuning in month six than it did in month one
 Longer term, full ownership of our paid creative
 The Bar 
 High expectations on volume, speed, and quality, all at the same time. This seat writes the ads that fund the business.
 If you want time to polish every line before anyone sees it, this is not the role. If you want your work in market within days and a scoreboard that tells you whether you were right, it is.
 What We're Looking For 
 Based in EE UU, Canada or the UK
 A direct response writer who thinks in awareness levels, mechanisms, and offers
 Experience writing spoken video ad scripts for cold paid traffic, with firsthand knowledge of how they performed
 The ability to provide creative direction for video, including scene direction, on-screen text, props, formats, and cuts
 Speed backed by a system: you are fast because you have built something that makes you fast
 Strong, defensible opinions about what stops the scroll
 Heavy content consumption and a sharp eye for why things work, including the ability to spot a format taking off on organic and translate it into an ad
 The ability to explain your thinking live to agency owners who have never written a hook
 Comfort using AI tools heavily as leverage while still producing genuinely strong original work
 The ability to learn new markets quickly and recognize when copy sounds wrong across industries
 Responsiveness throughout the working day and the ability to take feedback quickly and without ego
 Portfolio required: include at least one spoken video ad script and tell us what it achieved
 Nice to Have 
 YouTube or short-form organic scripts to share
 A concept you originated, along with the results it produced
 Fully remote role for candidates based in North America
 Clear compensation path: $5,500 USD/month to start, rising to $7,000 USD/month at full scope, with the targets written into your offer letter before you sign
 Paid trial projects: every trial project is paid, and you never write for us for free
 Direct work with the founders, both of whom have built and scaled agencies, one through to a sale
 Built-in leverage: a library of proven scripts, recorded sales calls, and AI tools and autonomous agents integrated into our systems
 Growth based on performance: no fixed waiting period to take on more of the founders' content, with a long-term path to owning our paid creative
 Fast feedback loop: your work goes into market within days, with real results to show what's working

Build the demand engine for Acuity’s next stage of growth. 
 Acuity Insights is entering a new stage of growth. We’ve spent years building products used by higher education programs to make important decisions about who enters their programs and how learners are supported once they get there. Today, established products are evolving, newer products are being commercialized, and we’re exploring how to reach new audiences and markets.
 As our Senior Growth Marketing Manager , you’ll help turn that opportunity into demand.
 You’re not walking into a blank slate, and you’re not inheriting a finished playbook. You’ll have enough foundation to move quickly and enough room to bring your own experience, ideas, and point of view to what comes next.
 You’ll have working campaigns, a strong webinar program, recurring prospect communications, established cross-functional partners, and improving data and measurement capabilities to build from.
 You’ll also have real whitespace. Nurture is a capability we need to build. International demand generation is largely unexplored. And we want you to bring the AI practices you’re already using in Growth Marketing to help accelerate our adoption, from campaign development and content repurposing to research, testing, and analysis. Across all of it, we want to get much better at understanding what creates qualified pipeline and contributes to revenue.
 You’ll be our only dedicated Growth Marketer, working hands-on across strategy and execution while surrounded by partners across Marketing and our broader Growth organization. This opportunity will suit you particularly well if you like getting close to the business, figuring out where marketing can have the greatest commercial impact, and turning that judgment into action.
 Before you apply: This is full-time, 16-month fixed-term employment covering an upcoming parental leave, open to candidates based anywhere in Canada. The start date is early November 2026. You’ll work remotely within Canada with access to employee benefits including healthcare coverage, paid time off, and a learning and development budget. 
 Thoughtful use of AI is welcome. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 You’ll start with Acuity’s company-wide onboarding program, building context on our business, products, customers, and how we work. From there, you’ll go deeper into Marketing and our broader Growth organization, getting close to the campaigns, data, priorities, relationships, and rhythms that shape Growth Marketing today.
 As you ramp, you’ll take increasing ownership of demand generation across our product portfolio, with the context and relationships you need to make good decisions and move independently.
 Take ownership of demand generation 
 You’ll set and run our quarterly demand-generation plans, deciding how Growth Marketing can best contribute to our commercial priorities and where to focus across competing opportunities.
 That means moving comfortably between strategy and execution: identifying the audiences and opportunities worth pursuing, choosing the right channels and tactics, building and launching the work, measuring what happens, and using what you learn to decide what comes next.
 You’ll have autonomy to bring your own judgment and experience to the work, while staying closely connected to the business priorities, product developments, and customer insights that should shape it.
 Turn product momentum into demand 
 You’ll work across a portfolio at different stages of maturity. Casper and One45 are established products with deep roots in higher education, with One45 now evolving into its next chapter. Video Interviews and Professional Skills Development are newer solutions we’re actively commercializing.
 Working with Product Marketing, Sales, Customer Success and Business Development, you’ll translate product positioning, market insight, customer needs, and commercialization priorities into demand-generation strategies that reach the right audiences and give them a reason to engage.
 You’ll gather context, develop a point of view about how Growth Marketing can contribute, recommend an approach, and carry it into market.
 Build demand across the funnel 
 You’ll architect, execute, and optimize integrated campaigns across the channels that make sense for the audience and opportunity, including paid media, email, web, content, prospect communications, and new approaches worth testing.
 You’ll continue building on a webinar program that has shown strong potential for generating qualified demand, owning the Growth Marketing motion end-to-end from audience and promotion strategy through registration, follow-up, and measurement.
 And you’ll build and evolve nurture programs beyond their current state: developing more intentional journeys for different audiences and verticals, identifying useful triggers and segmentation, and creating paths that help accelerate leads toward sales readiness.
 Get closer to what actually drives growth 
 You’ll help us become much more disciplined about asking: What worked? What generated qualified demand? What progressed into pipeline? What contributed to revenue? And what should we do differently next time?
 Using HubSpot, campaign data, and our evolving business intelligence capabilities, you’ll look beyond surface-level engagement metrics to understand how Growth Marketing contributes further down the funnel.
 You’ll establish stronger measurement rhythms, test targeting and messaging, compare performance across campaigns and channels, and use what you learn to make better decisions about where we invest our time and budget.
 You won’t control every downstream revenue outcome, but you’ll understand the connection between your work and the commercial funnel and take accountability for continuously improving that contribution.
 Put AI to work in Growth Marketing 
 You’ll bring AI practices that are already part of your toolkit and help us apply them meaningfully at Acuity. That could include campaign development, research, content creation and repurposing, nurture, experimentation, and analysis, as well as use cases we haven’t identified yet.
 The goal isn’t AI for its own sake. It’s finding practical ways to reduce manual work, get more leverage from what we create, improve quality and speed, and make better decisions. When something works, you’ll help turn it into a practice the broader team can learn from and continue using.
 Test how we generate demand internationally 
 As Acuity expands its international reach, you’ll help us learn how our demand-generation approach translates into priority market including Australia and New Zealand (ANZ), UK and Ireland.
 Working with partners across Growth, you’ll develop and run a focused demand-generation pilot in one of these markets. You’ll help determine the audience, messaging, channels, and measures of success, then use what happens in this market to build an evidence-based point of view about what we should test, change, or invest in next.
 Who You’ll Work With, and How
 You’ll report to our Director of Marketing and join a Marketing function that includes Marketing Operations, Digital Marketing, Customer Marketing, Events Marketing, Content and Communications.
 You’ll be our dedicated Growth Marketing expert. That means bringing your own expertise while knowing how to draw on the expertise around you.
 Sales and Business Development will be particularly important partners. They’re close to prospective customers every day and can help you understand the problems buyers are talking about, the language they use, what resonates, where opportunities are stalling, and what they’re hearing in the higher education market.
 You’ll collaborate with Customer Success to dig deeper into buyer insights, source speakers for virtual events, understand expansion opportunities, and amplify post-event follow-up.
 Your job is to listen closely, connect those insights with what you know about demand generation, and turn them into a point of view and a plan. Collaboration here doesn’t mean waiting for consensus or for someone else to tell you what campaign to run.
 You’ll work closely with Product Marketing to understand positioning, value propositions, audiences, and product messaging, then translate that foundation into campaigns and experiences designed for the people we want to reach.
 Within Marketing, you’ll collaborate with Customer Marketing, Events Marketing, Communications, Marketing Operations, and Creative teams to bring campaigns, customer proof points, thought leadership, webinars, and other experiences to life. 
 And with RevOps, you’ll strengthen the connection between marketing activity, lead progression, pipeline, and revenue so what we learn can shape what we do next.
 You won’t need to know everything yourself. You will need to know your craft, build strong relationships, ask good questions, make recommendations, and keep things moving.
 The Impact You’ll Have
 Over the course of your time with us, you’ll help build a stronger and more scalable demand-generation engine. Your impact will show up in:
 Greater commercial accountability. We’ll have clearer visibility into which campaigns, channels, audiences, and messages are creating qualified demand, progressing into pipeline, and contributing to revenue.
 A stronger nurture capability. We’ll have more intentional journeys for different audiences and verticals, giving promising demand more opportunities to progress toward sales readiness.
 Stronger commercialization. Professional Skills Development, Video Interviews, and the continued evolution of One45 will have focused demand-generation strategies supporting their growth in market.
 A more connected event-to-demand engine. Webinars and virtual events will connect more intentionally to follow-up, nurture, pipeline progression, and what we learn from each program.
 AI practices that create real leverage. We’ll have practical, proven ways of using AI to improve how Growth Marketing researches, creates, experiments, analyzes, and gets more from the work we produce.
 Evidence to inform international growth. We’ll have real market learnings from demand-generation experimentation in a priority international market, giving us a stronger foundation for what to test or invest in next.
 Across all of it, you’ll help us make growth decisions with more evidence and confidence, while leaving the demand engine stronger than you found it.
 How You’ll Succeed Here
 There’s no single profile for success in this role. But the person who thrives here will probably recognize themselves in a few things.
 You think commercially. 
Campaign activity is interesting to you because of what happens next. You want to understand whether people engaged, whether they became qualified opportunities, whether pipeline moved, and what that tells you about where to invest next.
 You bring a point of view. 
You listen to Sales, Business Development, Product, customer insights, market data,, but you don’t need everyone else to design the answer for you. You synthesize what you’ve learned, make recommendations, and move the work forward proactively.
 You know how to create momentum with what you have. 
You don’t need a huge budget, a large team, or a perfectly established playbook before you can make progress. You’re resourceful about figuring out what matters most, where to focus, and what you can build, test, or improve with the resources around you.
 You’re genuinely hands-on. 
You move fluidly between planning and doing, comfortably zooming out to set campaign strategy or diving into an ad platform, webinar plan, landing page, or email flow to make it real. You don't need a large team around you to move work forward. You can inherit something that already works, respect what has been built, and still see where it could become better.
 You experiment with purpose. 
You’re willing to try something new, but experimentation isn’t throwing ideas at a wall. You start with a hypothesis, look at what happened, learn from it, and decide whether to iterate, scale, or stop.
 You use AI as part of your craft. 
You’ve moved beyond simply being curious about AI. You’re already using it in your work, learning where it creates leverage, where human judgment matters, and how it can help you move faster or produce better work.
 You’re comfortable making choices. 
You've worked in environments where priorities evolve and the playbook isn't always complete. You bring structure, judgment, and a bias toward action while staying focused on measurable business impact. 
 Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running
 We care more about what you’ve actually owned, built, learned, and improved.
 You’ll likely bring experience: 
 Owning B2B demand generation with accountability for qualified leads, pipeline, and commercial outcomes, ideally in SaaS or another complex B2B environment.
 Personally designing, launching, measuring, and optimizing integrated campaigns across channels such as paid media, email, web, content, nurture, and virtual events.
 Bringing a new product or meaningful product development to market and building demand around it.
 Independently planning and executing webinars or other virtual events end to end, including content strategy, speaker sourcing, promotion, event flow, live execution, and post-event follow-up.
 Using marketing and funnel data to evaluate performance, identify patterns, make investment decisions, and understand how marketing activity contributes to pipeline and revenue.
 Building or significantly improving nurture programs, segmentation, automation flows, and recurring prospect communications using HubSpot or similar platforms.
 Partnering closely with Sales and Product Marketing to turn customer, market, and product insight into effective demand-generation strategies.
 Using AI meaningfully in your day-to-day marketing work to improve the quality, speed, analysis, or scale of what you produce.
 Experience generating demand outside North America, particularly in Australia/New Zealand or the UK/Ireland, would be valuable as we begin testing our approach in these markets.
 And if you’ve previously been the only Growth Marketer, or one of very few, you’ll bring particularly relevant experience for the level of ownership this role offers.
 How We Support You
 Transparent compensation. A salary between $110,000–$135,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
 Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, to deepen your expertise, build new skills, or explore new areas of interest.
 Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
 Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
 Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
 What Happens After You Apply
 We review every application carefully and don’t use AI to evaluate candidates, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements such as Canadian residency and valid work authorization. AI may support note-taking in some interviews, but people make every evaluation and hiring decision.
 Our interviews are two-way conversations: a chance for us to understand your experience and what you’re looking for, and for you to get to know Acuity, the role, and the people you’d work with. The process typically takes 2–4 weeks from first conversation to final decision.
 Steps in the Process
 Application Review. A member of our Talent team reviews your application.
 Intro Conversation. You’ll meet with a member of our Talent team to explore your experience, what you’re looking for next, and learn more broadly about Acuity Insights and the opportunity. 
 Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Director of Marketing to dig into the growth work you’ve owned, the decisions you’ve made, and the results. If you have something you can share, we’ll invite you to bring an example of real work you’re proud of so we can explore how you approached it and what you learned.
 Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and move work forward, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
 Decision. We bring together feedback from your conversations and typically make a decision within 2–4 business days.
 Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.
 Life at Acuity Insights
 We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.
 Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.
 Day to day, you can expect:
 High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done
 Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team
 Space for focused work alongside intentional collaboration and connection
 Colleagues who are generous with their expertise and expect you to bring yours
 A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness
 As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions and do work they’re proud of.
 About Acuity Insights
 Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.
 Our work is grounded in a simple idea: that people are more than their grades, and that potential can be understood and developed, not just measured.
 Our Casper situational judgment test (SJT), created by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is one of the most widely used open-response SJTs in higher education, backed by nearly 20 years of research.
 Today, we are evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions not just identify potential, but actively support its growth over time. As part of that evolution, we’re increasingly building toward a more connected ecosystem across assessment, education, and learner development. While teams remain focused on their individual products, we’re creating stronger connections across our platform to deliver more cohesive experiences for institutions and learners.

About the Role
We are looking for a Self-Driving Systems Specialist (SDS Specialist) to support the diagnostics, calibration, configuration, and technical readiness of self-driving systems used in autonomous vehicles and robotaxi fleets across North America.
The SDS Specialist focuses on the technology layer of autonomous mobility: sensors, compute systems, software configurations, autonomous driving hardware, system diagnostics, calibration procedures, and technical validation. This role ensures that the self-driving system installed in each autonomous vehicle is functioning correctly, accurately calibrated, and ready to support safe testing, commercial deployment, and autonomous ride-hailing operations.
You will work closely with Senior Technicians, AV Operations Leads, Safety Operators, Depot Specialists, engineering teams, and fleet operations teams to identify technical issues, execute structured troubleshooting procedures, and support reliable operation of autonomous vehicle platforms.
This position is ideal for candidates with experience in automotive electronics, ADAS systems, embedded systems, robotics, diagnostics, calibration, or complex technical support who want to work at the center of autonomous vehicle deployment and robotaxi operations.

Key Responsibilities: Self-Driving System Diagnostics 
 Diagnose and troubleshoot self-driving system issues affecting autonomous vehicle performance and fleet readiness.
 Investigate technical problems related to cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS/GNSS, compute units, sensors, connectivity modules, wiring, and autonomous driving hardware.
 Execute structured diagnostic procedures to identify root causes of SDS hardware, software, and configuration issues.
 Support advanced troubleshooting for autonomous vehicle faults that impact testing, commercial operations, or robotaxi fleet availability .
 Escalate complex technical cases to engineering teams with clear findings and supporting documentation.
 Hardware Support 
 Inspect, repair, replace, and validate SDS hardware components installed on autonomous vehicles.
 Support installation and verification of cameras, LiDAR units, radar sensors, compute hardware, sensor mounts, antennas, and related components.
 Confirm that autonomous driving hardware is correctly installed, secured, clean, functional, and ready for operation.
 Collaborate with Senior Technicians on vehicle-level issues involving both standard automotive systems and SDS components.
 Ensure all hardware work is completed according to strict safety, quality, and technical procedures.
 Software Configuration & Updates 
 Perform software updates, configuration changes, and system validation checks for autonomous driving systems.
 Execute defined software procedures using diagnostic tools, command-line tools, configuration files, or engineering-provided workflows.
 Verify successful software installation and confirm that the SDS is operational before the vehicle returns to service.
 Support troubleshooting of software-related issues affecting autonomous vehicle behavior, system communication, or operational readiness.
 Maintain accurate records of software versions, configurations, updates, and validation results.
 Sensor Calibration & Validation 
 Perform calibration and verification activities for autonomous vehicle sensors and self-driving system components.
 Support calibration workflows involving cameras, LiDAR, radar, localization systems, and other perception-related hardware.
 Validate that the self-driving system is functioning correctly after maintenance, software updates, hardware replacement, or vehicle service.
 Assist engineering teams with data collection, calibration testing, and system performance verification.
 Ensure autonomous vehicles meet technical readiness requirements before returning to robotaxi operations or on-road testing.
 Engineering & Operations Support 
 Serve as the on-site subject matter expert for SDS-related technical issues.
 Provide structured technical findings to engineering, fleet operations, and project teams.
 Collaborate with AV Operations Leads to prioritize SDS-related repairs and reduce vehicle downtime.
 Support incident reviews, root-cause analysis, and technical escalation processes.
 Contribute to continuous improvement of troubleshooting workflows, calibration procedures, and operational documentation.
 Documentation & Compliance 
 Maintain accurate records of diagnostics, repairs, software updates, hardware changes, and calibration activities.
 Follow strict operational, safety, and technical procedures when working with autonomous driving systems.
 Complete all required system validation checklists and technical reports.
 Support compliance with internal quality standards, safety protocols, and customer requirements.
 Ensure all SDS-related work is traceable, repeatable, and properly documented.
Requirements: Essential 
 Minimum 3+ years of experience in automotive electronics, diagnostics, embedded systems, robotics, technical support, or complex technical systems.
 Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills.
 Experience working with vehicle electronics, sensors, control systems, or advanced technical hardware.
 Comfortable following structured software procedures and technical workflows.
 Ability to work with diagnostic tools, logs, technical documentation, and engineering instructions.
 High attention to detail and strong procedural discipline.
 Good communication skills and ability to work with cross-functional technical teams.
 Fluent English.
 Strongly Preferred 
 Experience with ADAS , autonomous vehicles, robotics, sensor systems, or advanced driver assistance technologies.
 Familiarity with LiDAR, radar, camera systems, GNSS, IMU, compute units, or perception-related hardware.
 Experience with Linux, command-line tools, CAN bus, vehicle networks, or embedded systems.
 Experience performing calibration, validation, or system integration activities.
 Background in automotive testing, AV operations, robotics labs, fleet diagnostics, or technical field support.
What We Are Looking For: Successful SDS Specialists are precise, structured, and technically curious. They enjoy solving complex system problems and understand that reliable self-driving system performance is essential for safe autonomous vehicle operations , commercial robotaxi services , and fleet scaling.
 This role requires someone who can work carefully with advanced hardware and software, follow engineering procedures exactly, and communicate findings clearly to both technical and operational teams. You should be comfortable working in a depot or technical operations environment where autonomous vehicles must be diagnosed, validated, and returned to service quickly and safely.
What We Offer: Opportunity to work directly with self-driving systems , autonomous driving hardware, and advanced vehicle technologies.
 Hands-on involvement in robotaxi fleet operations , autonomous vehicle testing , and autonomous ride-hailing deployment across North America.
 Exposure to robotics, ADAS, sensor calibration, embedded systems, EV platforms, and next-generation mobility technologies.
 Structured onboarding, technical procedures, and ongoing training.
 Career development opportunities in autonomous vehicle operations, AV diagnostics, robotics, and technical fleet support.
 Collaboration with engineering, operations, depot, technician, and safety teams.
 Opportunity to support new city launches , fleet scaling, and commercial autonomous mobility programs.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 POSITION SUMMARY    
 The Board-Certified Behaviour Analyst provides clinical supervision to frontline clinicians and consultation for complex clinical intervention, including intrusive behavioural intervention strategies. Services will include assessment, treatment and therapeutic programming, clinical consultation, program evaluation, training, education, and research activities within a variety of settings throughout CHEO’s region of Eastern Ontario including homes, community settings and group homes. Travel, and evening and weekend work should be an expectation of the position 
 LOCATION   
 This position serves the Eastern Catchment area . The successful candidate must reside in the region or be willing to travel within the area during their own time and at their own expense. 
 MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES     
 Develop, monitor, and evaluate therapeutic treatment interventions utilizing evidence-based ABA practices. Ensure that process for evidenced based practice is implemented in all areas of service delivery.   
 Provide consultation services to individuals and groups such as: clients, relatives of clients, professional associations, agency staff, mental health workers, and involved medical providers. 
 Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings, committees (internal and external) and initiatives designed to support the clients, families, direct care staff, and community partners. 
 Represent CHEO on internal and external clinical review committees as required in the area of behaviour practices and ABA.   
  Provide clinical oversight and accountability for the delivery of ABA-based service and provide clinical supervision to Behaviour therapists for ABA-Based case conceptualization, assessment, and treatment, in accordance with College of Psychologists and Behaviour Analysts of Ontario’s Standards of Professional Conduct, 2024 
  Engage in clinical supervision activities which includes, but is not limited to, describing theoretical orientation for assessment and treatment decisions, reviewing and discussion of written materials, reviewing client progress, data collection and graphing, video and/or in-situ observation, role play, discussion of literature and ethical dilemmas, and providing clinical feedback anchored in Behaviour Therapist’s clinical competencies.  
  Meet with Behaviour Therapists regularly to enable active monitoring of goals and progress concerning each service recipient and provide continuous planning, monitoring and evaluating of clinical practice. 
 Maintain records of clinical supervision activities and contacts with Behaviour Therapists.  
 Develop and provide formal staff training in skill acquisition methodologies and techniques to support problem behaviour (i.e. aggression, self-injury, property destruction) 
 Prepare and maintain formal documentation including but not limited to assessment reports, treatment plans, program plans, guidelines, program review summaries, and discharge summaries, electronic records charting, session progress notes, strategy recommendations, consent forms, supervision review summaries, and email communication with the family and care team (including external providers).   
 As part of clinical supervision, review and co-sign all behaviour analytic documents which may be reasonably relied upon to make a decision affecting client care, rights, and welfare, including but not limited to the documents identified above. 
 Manage own schedule after given assignments by corresponding with families and other professionals to schedule client consultations/ appointments/groups/interpreters and meetings and then booking the appointments in the electronic booking system sending invites and maintaining outlook calendars on a daily basis. Travelling to clients as required. 
 Perform work in accordance with the provisions of the Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulations and all CHEO corporate/departmental policies and procedures related to Occupational Health and Safety. 
 As per the regulation of the practice of Applied Behaviour Analysis and associated Standards of Professional Conduct, 2024, clinical supervision structure must involve the following: 
 Clients receiving supervised services are the supervisor’s clients. All professional responsibilities regarding supervision flow from this fundamental premise 
 Supervisors must assess the knowledge, skills and competence of their supervisees and provide supervision as appropriate to their assessments. 
 Regularly review the list of active clients and actively monitor all matters to determine the optimal frequency of discussion of each client. 
 Maintaining records of clinical supervision activities and contacts with Behaviour Therapists, which must include outlining date and duration of supervision meeting, summary of discussions and directives given to the Behaviour Therapist and the Behaviour Therapist’s strengths and developmental needs.  
 Supervision must be sufficiently intensive to enable active monitoring of goals and progress concerning each service recipient. The expected frequency and duration of supervision meetings will be under the discretion of the supervising Behaviour Analyst, in order to provide continuous planning, monitoring and evaluating of clinical practice, and to ensure compliance with all relevant legislation, regulations, and the Standards of Professional Conduct, 2024.  
 Perform other related duties as required and assigned. 
 QUALIFICATIONS     
 Master’s degree of Applied Disabilities Studies, Psychology or in a related field (Essential) 
 Five (5) years recent related experience in a behavioural management consultant position or equivalent experience (e.g., five years recent experience in Applied Behaviour Analysis in community program for persons with a developmental delay). (Essential) 
 Previous experience providing clinical supervision (Essential) 
 Maintain good standing as a Registered Behaviour Analyst with the College of Psychologists and Behaviour Analysts of Ontario (Essential) 
 Meet all eligibility requirements for being a listed as a qualified provider on the Ontario Autism Program Provider list as of April 2021 or in the process of obtaining. (Essential) 
 Current First Aid/CPR Certification (Essential)  
 Advanced knowledge of Applied Behaviour Analysis and its application. (Essential) 
 Clinical skills that demonstrate competence in assessment with children, youths and their families. (Essential) 
 Demonstrated leadership, coaching and mentoring skills. (Essential) 
 Strong interpersonal and communication skills, ability to receive and incorporate feedback. (Essential) 
 Knowledge of community resources for children and youth with special needs. (Essential) 
 Computer literacy with clinical applications (especially Microsoft office, Excel). (Essential) 
 Ability to provide services in a culturally sensitive environment. (Essential)

EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT TO THE CEO
 Fully remote | Full-time, 1099/ contractor | Monday–Friday, US Eastern Time business hours, with availability for urgent items
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 A fast-growing, founder-led company is hiring a remote Executive Assistant to work directly alongside its CEO.
 The CEO is growing fast on social media, personally runs the company's highest-value sales, and is also the creative strategist on client ad accounts. This role exists to remove those bottlenecks: organize him, protect his time and keep everything moving, so he can focus on content and on selling to high-net-worth clients.
 This is not a passive support role. The CEO wants a partner who builds the structure, holds him to it and tells him what he needs to hear.
 The single goal of this role is to buy back the CEO's time.
 This role is focused on the business. Household and family logistics are handled by a separate on-site Life Manager.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Calendar and priorities
 - Own and defend the CEO's calendar. Build the day around his highest-value work (content, high-value sales calls, consultations) and hold him to it.
 - Run a daily priority list so nothing important gets pushed aside by noise.
 - Triage the inbox and messages: handle what you can, flag what needs him, and close loops.
 Removing bottlenecks
 - Track every deliverable, approval and decision waiting on the CEO, including creative strategy for client ad accounts, and drive turnaround so client work does not stall.
 - Act as the single intake point for company reporting: collect, review and present short digests instead of passing raw reports through.
 - Coordinate follow-ups across the team so approvals and decisions keep moving.
 Sales, content and offers support
 - Schedule and prepare high-value sales calls, consultations and coaching calls: briefing notes beforehand, CRM updates and follow-ups afterwards.
 - Keep the social media content pipeline on schedule: recording blocks, coordination with editors and the team, and the publishing calendar.
 - Support the launch and delivery of new offers (coaching, consultations): scheduling, documents and logistics.
 Travel and administration
 - Book business travel and build itineraries.
 - Handle business admin: documents, agreements, expense tracking.
 Systems and tools
 - Build and maintain the operating layer: trackers, SOPs, checklists and recurring process documentation.
 - Expected fluency: Google Workspace, Slack, a project management tool (ClickUp, Notion or equivalent), a CRM, spreadsheets, and daily use of AI assistants.
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
 In the first 90 days you have taken the calendar, inbox triage and reporting flow off the CEO's plate, there is a live tracker of everything waiting on him, and client creative work no longer sits on his desk for weeks.
 By 6–12 months you are the CEO's right hand: the business runs on a weekly rhythm you built, nothing depends on him remembering it, and his time goes to content and high-value sales.
 IDEAL CANDIDATE
 - 3+ years as an Executive Assistant, Chief of Staff or equivalent to a founder, CEO or senior executive, ideally in a fast-growing or entrepreneurial company.
 - Proven remote experience: you have run an executive's day without being in the room.
 - Fluent professional English, written and spoken.
 - Able to work US Eastern Time business hours consistently, with reliable internet and a quiet workspace.
 - Strong administrative and operational backbone. You build systems, you don't just follow them.
 - Exceptional discretion with confidential business and financial information.
 - Tech-savvy: you master Google Workspace, Slack, a project management tool (ClickUp, Notion or equivalent), a CRM, spreadsheets, and daily use of AI assistants.
 You will thrive here if
 - You are direct, unflappable and comfortable with a straightforward, high-energy, fast-moving principal. Feedback is candid and immediate, and nothing is personal.
 - You are willing to push back and tell the CEO what he needs to hear. He wants a partner who holds him accountable, not someone who waits for instructions.
 - You are energized by walking into disorder and creating structure.
 Nice to have
 - Experience in a marketing agency, paid ads or creative production environment.
 - Social media or content operations experience.
 - Experience supporting a founder who sells coaching, consulting or premium offers.
 WHY THIS ROLE
 - Employment type: full-time 1099 independent contractor
 - Paid Time Off and fully remote
 - Growth: direct mentorship from the CEO and a clear path to grow into a Chief of Staff position
 - Network: exposure to high-impact leaders
 Complete discretion and confidentiality are required. The people who succeed in this seat enjoy managing complexity and operate with a high level of ownership in a dynamic, sometimes chaotic environment.

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Toronto team and help us take our products to the next level in terms of visual intelligence. 
 Our Company  
 Invision AI is building a universal AI platform for computer vision applications. Powered by a unique multi-camera stack that generates high-integrity 3D digital twins of dynamic environments, our technology powers disruptive, market-leading solutions in intelligent infrastructure and global Transportation. 
 The Role 
 As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will work across the full machine learning lifecycle, from data collection and labeling strategy through training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and ongoing improvement.
 Your focus will be developing and maintaining computer vision models used in real-world products. While the work may involve researching and implementing new approaches, this is primarily an applied engineering position. We are looking for someone with a track record of building, shipping, and maintaining production ML systems.
 The position includes working on projects that expand and strengthen our capabilities in object detection, image classification, geospatial tracking, and sensor fusion, with models deployed to resource-constrained edge devices.
 Working within a collaborative team, you will build accurate, efficient, and principled solutions. As a key contributor to the company's next stage of growth, you will help advance our products, solve challenging customer problems, and shape our ML engineering practices in a fast-moving environment.
 Location 
 This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Toronto. You will work from our downtown Toronto office three days per week.
 What You'll Do 
 Recommend, develop, evaluate, and deploy ML models across our product lines
 Build and improve data-labeling, training, and evaluation pipelines
 Establish evaluation methods that connect model performance to product and business outcomes
 Prototype new product capabilities using appropriate technologies
 Optimize models for latency, memory usage, power consumption, and accuracy on edge devices
 Diagnose and resolve issues affecting deployed models
 Monitor production performance and identify model drift, data-quality problems, and retraining needs
 Write maintainable, well-tested code and clear technical documentation
 Participate in design reviews, code reviews, and technical planning
 Share ML knowledge and collaborate with software, product, and other engineering teams
 Must Have 
 A track record of developing and deploying production computer vision models
 Strong Python software development skills
 Proficiency with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and scikit-learn
 Practical knowledge of CNNs and modern computer vision architectures
 The ability to adapt open-source models to specific products and use cases
 Hands-on work optimizing models for resource-constrained or edge environments
 Knowledge of experiment tracking, dataset versioning, and ML observability
 Skill in designing evaluation metrics that reflect product and business requirements
 An understanding of model monitoring and production troubleshooting
 Working knowledge of embedded systems and their constraints
 Sound software engineering practices, including automated testing, code review, version control, and continuous integration
 Strong written and verbal communication skills
 Must be legally entitled to work in Canada
 Bonus Skills 
 Familiarity with Docker or other container technologies
 C++ development skills
 GPU programming or performance-optimization knowledge
 Knowledge of model compression techniques, including quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation
 Familiarity with edge inference tools such as ONNX Runtime, TensorRT
 Familiarity with traditional, non-ML image-processing techniques
 A background in sensor fusion or geospatial data
